title: [CQ-I04] VS Code contract parity
description:
Objective: Mirror revision-safe review, profile settings and shared evidence status in secondary client.

Deliverable: VS Code contract parity. This is task I04 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): I02.
definitionOfDone: All board/detail approve paths pass rendered revision.
Wire defaults do not weaken strict settings.
Fresh verification `cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
Fix only moe-vscode/src/panels/PlanReviewPanel.ts so that success is bound to the reviewed revision. This mirrors I02's PlanReviewApprovalState.onStateUpdate.

(a) Add a module-private helper next to isPlanRevision. Do not export it:
    function effectivePlanRevision(task: Task): number | undefined { const raw: unknown = task.planRevision; if (raw === undefined) { return 0; } return isPlanRevision(raw) ? raw : undefined; }
   An absent field is the legacy effective 0, which is exactly how the daemon reads it. A present malformed value is unusable and is never coerced. Leave seedRevisionAttribute, isPlanRevision and showApprovalRefusal byte-identical: TaskDetailPanel imports them, and peer vm harnesses load this module.

(b) Add `private settlePendingApproval(): void`. It is now the ONLY success path, and its comment says success means WORKING at the SAME revision the human approved. Logic:
   - Return when disposed or when pendingApprovalRevision is undefined, before any task lookup.
   - Find the task; return unless it exists with status 'WORKING'.
   - If effectivePlanRevision(task) === pending: clear pending, call showInformationMessage('Plan approved'), dispose(), and return.
   - Otherwise (another revision, or an unusable one): showWarningMessage. For a numeric revision the text is `Plan approval not confirmed: work started on plan revision ${current}, not revision ${pending} that you reviewed.`. For an unusable one it is `Plan approval not confirmed: work started on a plan whose revision is unreadable.`. Then call `void this.reportApprovalFailure(true, <same text>)`, which clears pending synchronously and latches the page with its existing stale notice.
   - Never assign the new revision to pending, never retry, and never read a token from the cache for sending.

(c) Call it from the onStateChanged subscription on EVERY state event, before the render debounce: `this.client.onStateChanged(() => { this.settlePendingApproval(); this.debouncedUpdate(); })`. debouncedUpdate already returns when disposed. MoeDaemonClient applies each daemon frame to currentState before firing, so the first WORKING frame at the reviewed revision is seen even when a later frame (a step start that bumps planRevision) lands within the 200ms debounce.

(d) Delete the old any-WORKING branch inside the debounce timer. The timer keeps only the taskRemoved path and postTaskUpdate. Move the 'ONLY authoritative completion' comment to the new method.

Keep the existing error handling unchanged: handleClientError, handleConnectionChange, the duplicate-click gate, contentOutOfSync and the approvePending/approveFailed control messages. Do not change media/planReview.js: its stale approveFailed already latches the page for good, and a later non-stale failure keeps it latched. Add no imports (the vm test harnesses use strict require maps). Make step 1 green without editing any test, keep LF line endings, and aim for about +30/-8 lines.

Pin DoD 2 (wire defaults do not weaken strict settings) in a NEW file, moe-vscode/tests/settings-wire.test.cjs. The name must end in .test.cjs so that `node --test tests/*.test.cjs` collects it. These are guard tests that should pass against today's code; their value comes from the mutation proof below. This step edits no production file. If a case fails on today's code, stop and report it in the step note; never loosen the assertion.

Harness: inline, about 70 lines, modelled on tests/plan-approval-client.test.cjs and tests/plan-review.test.cjs. No shared helper file and no new dependency.
- Transpile src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts and src/panels/SettingsPanel.ts with ts.transpileModule (CommonJS, ES2020, esModuleInterop). Read media/settings.js raw.
- Use a fresh vm context per test. SettingsPanel.currentPanel is static, so reusing a context would hit reveal.
- Require maps throw on any unexpected name. The client gets vscode; ws (a constructor stub with OPEN 1 that throws if constructed); child_process (throws on spawn); fs; path; net. The panel gets vscode only.
- Use one plain top-level vscode object, not a strict Proxy: esModuleInterop's __importStar probes it. It provides:
  - EventEmitter (the recording emitter);
  - ViewColumn.One and Uri.joinPath;
  - workspace.getConfiguration, whose get returns false (keeps autoConnect off, so no reconnect timers);
  - window.createOutputChannel;
  - window.createWebviewPanel, returning a fake panel. Its webview has cspSource, an identity asWebviewUri, an html field, and an onDidReceiveMessage that captures the handler. The panel counts onDidDispose, reveal and dispose calls;
  - recorders for showInformationMessage and showErrorMessage.
- Construct the REAL client with `new MoeDaemonClient('extension')`. Inject `client['ws'] = { readyState: 1, send: frame => frames.push(JSON.parse(frame)), close() {} }` and set `client['_connectionState'] = 'connected'`. Deliver the snapshot through `client['handleMessage'](JSON.stringify({ type: 'STATE_SNAPSHOT', payload }))`, then open with `SettingsPanel.createOrShow('ext', client, client.currentState)`, exactly as extension.ts does.
- Build the page realm from the HTML the panel emitted:
  - collect input, select and button opening tags by id; getElementById returns null for any id not in that HTML, and never auto-creates elements;
  - an input's value is its value attribute, decoded from the five escapeHtml entities (decode the ampersand last);
  - the checkbox is checked only if its opening tag carries the checked attribute;
  - the select's value is the option marked selected, else the first option (browser default);
  - elements record click listeners, and acquireVsCodeApi().postMessage forwards to the captured panel handler.
- Assert on frames JSON-parsed in the test realm, which avoids cross-realm deepEqual failures. Dispose the client in finally. Every harness failure (missing id, missing handler, unexpected require) throws a clear test error.

Fixture STORED: the six form keys with non-default values: approvalMode 'CONTROL'; speedModeDelayMs 4500; an agentCommand containing a double quote, an ampersand and a less-than sign; autoCreateBranch false; branchPattern 'moe/{taskId}-x'; a commitPattern containing an apostrophe. Add these strict and unrelated keys: executionProfile 'observe', deliveryPolicy 'local-branch', qualityGate 'npm test', qualityGateScope 'everyTask', consolidationBranch 'moe/work-*', autoCommit false, checkpointCommits false, checkpointPush false, commitBoardState false, commitHooks true, attribution { undeclared: 'never', contested: 'skip' }, taskSizing { maxSteps: 6 }, appendOnlyFiles ['CHANGELOG.md'], refusalCascadeAutoBacklog false, enableAgentTeams true, chatEnabled false, chatMaxAgentHops 2, columnLimits { WORKING: 2 }. FORM_KEYS = agentCommand, approvalMode, autoCreateBranch, branchPattern, commitPattern, speedModeDelayMs.

Cases:
- S1, an unedited save writes back exactly the stored form values. Click saveBtn. Expect exactly one frame of type 'UPDATE_SETTINGS', Object.keys(payload).sort() deepEqual to FORM_KEYS, and every value strictly equal to STORED[key] (speedModeDelayMs is the number 4500). No other STORED key may appear in the payload. Expect the info toast 'Settings saved.' and one panel dispose.
- S2, a table over approvalMode CONTROL, SPEED and TURBO. An unedited save sends the stored mode unchanged, so the form can neither weaken CONTROL nor rewrite another mode.
- S3, a snapshot with no project at all. The form defaults reach the wire as approvalMode 'CONTROL' (the strictest mode), speedModeDelayMs 2000, agentCommand 'claude', autoCreateBranch true, branchPattern 'moe/{epicId}/{taskId}' and commitPattern 'feat({epicId}): {taskTitle}'. The key set is exactly FORM_KEYS, so no default for executionProfile, deliveryPolicy or any other strict key is invented.
- S4, user edits reach the wire as typed: approvalMode SPEED; delay '3000'; agentCommand '  grok  ', trimmed to 'grok'; autoCreateBranch checked; branchPattern edited with surrounding spaces, then trimmed. The untouched commitPattern stays STORED's value, and the key set is still FORM_KEYS.
- S5, a table over a delay of '', 'abc' and '0'. The payload carries the number 2000, never 0, NaN or null; a 0ms delay would make SPEED approve instantly.

Mutation proof: use a scratch copy outside the repo with the same moe-vscode/{media,src/panels,src/services,tests} layout, run with NODE_PATH=<repo>/moe-vscode/node_modules, apply one exact replacement per mutant with a count==1 assert, then delete the scratch dir.
- m1: change SettingsPanel's approvalMode fallback from 'CONTROL' to 'TURBO'. S3 goes red.
- m2: add `executionProfile: 'legacy',` to the save object. S1, S3 and S4 go red.
- m3: change settings.js `|| 2000` to `|| 0`. S5 goes red.
- m4: make MoeDaemonClient.updateSettings send `{ ...(this.state?.project?.settings ?? {}), ...settings }`. S1 goes red.
Record each mutant's red test names in the step note. Budget about 170 lines for this file.

Single verification gate, run once after steps 1-3. From the repository root, run exactly `cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile` fresh, and keep the command, exitCode and outputTail for complete_task.
- Expect node:test totals of the previous 134 plus every new test (about 26), with 0 failed, cancelled or skipped, and tsc exit 0.
- This covers DoD 3: the daemon-start startup tests, the existing approval-paths, plan-approval-client, plan-review and task-* suites, and the typecheck all stay green.
- Linux, macOS and WSL run the command as written. On Windows cmd, use `cmd /d /c "cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile"`.
- moe-vscode/node_modules must already be installed. Do not reinstall or upgrade packages to get around an environment failure; report it instead.
- compile writes only moe-vscode/dist, which is gitignored.
- This is a VS Code-only change with no shared schema, protocol or daemon edit, so no other package suite is required here. I06 owns whole-epic integration and docs.

One final adversarial self-review (adversarial-self-review skill), limited to the three owned files. Check:
1. An approval followed by a newer, older, zero, legacy-missing or malformed WORKING never shows 'Plan approved', never closes the panel, and never re-arms.
2. A same-revision WORKING (0, 4, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, legacy-missing) closes exactly once, even when a later revision lands inside the debounce.
3. Both error/WORKING orders, duplicate clicks, a disconnect while pending, and dispose mid-flight still behave as the existing tests say.
4. The per-event path costs nothing when no approval is pending: it returns early, before any task lookup.
5. No token is ever read from cached state for sending.
6. DoD 1 audit: run `grep -n -E "approveTask|updateTaskStatus\(|APPROVE_TASK" -r moe-vscode/src moe-vscode/media`. Confirm every approval-capable route is still the F04d set (detail Approve and Next, board card, board drag and epic sweep, plan review), each with a covering test in approval-paths.test.cjs or plan-review.test.cjs. Report any new route instead of fixing it here.
7. The settings payload is still exactly the six form keys.

Size: `git diff --numstat -- moe-vscode` plus `wc -l` of the new test file must stay under 400 net changed lines, which is QA's review cap with tests counted; the target is 360 or fewer. Compress tables before dropping any enumerated case.

If any byte changes after step 4, re-run the mutants from steps 1-3, then re-run the step 4 command and use that fresh output.

Rules: no Git writes and no direct .moe edits. Do not edit media/planReview.js, SettingsPanel.ts, settings.js or MoeDaemonClient.ts. Leave peer and pre-existing dirty bytes untouched. Finish with complete_task and the fresh gate output.

comments.content:
Architect scope note (architect-4c57a52b, 2026-10-26). I04 mirrors what I02 actually shipped after the human's REPL clarification on I02: "Focus on approvals; preserve existing settings and status UI".

1. Approve routes (DoD 1): CQ-F04d (cb7b75f4) already sends the rendered revision from every VS Code route: detail Approve and Next, board card, board drag, epic sweep, and plan review. tests/approval-paths.test.cjs pins all of them. Nothing is reworked; the final review step re-audits the routes.
2. Remaining revision-safety gap (I02 parity): while an approval is pending, PlanReviewPanel shows "Plan approved" and closes on ANY WORKING update, before it checks the revision. The plan accepts only WORKING at the SAME reviewed revision. It checks on every state event rather than after the 200ms render debounce, so a step start that bumps the revision cannot hide a real approval. Any other revision, or an unreadable one, warns and latches the page.
3. Settings (DoD 2): no production change. The save sends exactly six form keys, and the daemon merges partial updates, so executionProfile, deliveryPolicy and every other strict key survive. The approval-mode default is CONTROL, and the form never sends a 0ms delay. A new real-client wire test pins all of this, with mutation proof.

Out of scope, and why:
- CLIENT_HELLO negotiation: JetBrains sends none, JetBrains-first applies, and CQ-F04b already refuses token-free approval.
- Profile/evidence status UI: it was dropped for I02. The VS Code profile round trip is in I05's DoD, and evidence status needs an owner that depends on V06.

Noticed, not fixed here: SettingsPanel ignores the result of updateSettings and shows "Settings saved." even while disconnected, and a daemon refusal of UPDATE_SETTINGS is only logged. That is a separate bug for the governor to route.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Scope follows what I02 shipped after the human's REPL clarification on I02: 'Focus on approvals; preserve existing settings and status UI'. The scope note is in task comment comment-17879d71.

Rejected:
(a) CLIENT_HELLO negotiation in VS Code. JetBrains sends none, the JetBrains-first rule forbids VS Code leading, CQ-F04b already refuses token-free approval, and no DoD item asks for it.
(b) Profile/evidence status UI. It was dropped for I02. The VS Code profile round trip is I05's DoD ('No profile/evidence fields are discarded in settings roundtrip'), and evidence status needs an owner that depends on V06.
(c) task.approvedPlanRevision as the success witness. I02 compares planRevision, and an older daemon without the stamp would never confirm. A per-event check removes the debounce race instead.
(d) A host-side invalidation latch duplicating the page latch. The page latch plus the daemon CAS already make re-approval impossible.
(e) Settings production changes. They are not needed: the six-key payload plus the daemon's partial merge preserve every strict key, the approval-mode default is CONTROL, and the delay can never be 0.

The approve routes were already moved to the rendered revision by CQ-F04d (cb7b75f4) and are not reworked.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Goal: VS Code parity with CQ-I02's revision-bound approval acknowledgement, plus a wire pin for the settings save.

Gap: PlanReviewPanel.debouncedUpdate ends a pending approval on ANY WORKING task, before it checks the revision.

Daemon facts: taskStore.approveTask writes only status and planApprovedAt, so approval leaves planRevision unchanged and stamps approvedPlanRevision. Later plan or step writes may bump planRevision.

Client facts: MoeDaemonClient applies each frame to currentState before firing onStateChanged, so a per-event check sees the first WORKING frame.

Page facts (media/planReview.js): approveFailed with stale:true latches the page for good with PLAN_CHANGED_NOTICE. A later non-stale approveFailed keeps it latched.

Test harness facts:
- tests/plan-review.test.cjs: pushUpdate is setTasks + emitState + flushTimers. emitState alone does not flush the debounce. Fake timer ids start at 1, and RecordingEventEmitter fires over a copy of its listener list.
- tests/plan-approval-client.test.cjs shows how to load the real client in a vm and inject a socket.
- approval-paths.test.cjs loads the real PlanReviewPanel with a require map that allows only vscode, so the fix must add no imports.

Settings facts: SettingsPanel sends approvalMode, speedModeDelayMs, agentCommand, autoCreateBranch, branchPattern and commitPattern. settings.js maps an unparseable or zero delay to 2000. The daemon's validateSettingsUpdate merges partial input into the stored settings.
planningNotes.risks:
LOC: QA enforces a 400 net-changed-line cap with tests counted, and no CQ-I rail waives it. The budget is 360 or fewer: about 30 production lines, about 130 in plan-review tests and about 170 in the settings test.

Test pitfalls:
- vm-realm objects fail deepStrictEqual. Compare JSON-parsed frames or spread copies.
- A settings harness that auto-creates elements proves nothing.

Behaviour notes:
- Real VS Code EventEmitter tolerates a listener disposing during fire, and dispose() is already idempotent.
- A WORKING mismatch followed by a correlated refusal yields two toasts by design (the new warning plus the existing error report). Tests assert only the invariants.

Out of scope, noted: SettingsPanel ignores the result of updateSettings, so it shows 'Settings saved.' even while disconnected, and a daemon refusal of UPDATE_SETTINGS is only logged. That is a separate bug for the governor.

State at planning: moe-vscode was clean. 554 peer or pre-existing dirty paths elsewhere stay untouched. Baseline on WSL: npm test 134/134 pass, compile exit 0, about 7s.
